| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |\n\n**Eval result ingestion** (`/projects/{project
Id}/eval-ingest/...`) — how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval runs executed outside the platform (local dev, CI). The `{projec
tId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users never call these directly — set `MCPJAM_

API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| -
| - |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and finalize it |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/r
uns/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/iterations` | A
ppend an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (idempotent) |\n| `PO
ST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) and return its `storageId` |
\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcp
jam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\n**Agent** (`/projects/{projectId}/ag

ent`) — a headless assistant turn for
building conversational surfaces (the MCPJam Slack app is the first consumer):

| Endpoin
t | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: \"user\"\\|\"assista
nt\", content}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the project. The t
urn can read project servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs — kick those off yourself with `POST ..
./eval-runs`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), and token `usage
`. Capped at 4 concurrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent — never blind-retry**: dedupe on your ow
n trigger identity, and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list suites) before ret

rying, or you'll create duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | -
|\n| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .../studi
es/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it publishes,
and its insights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null |\n\n>

[!NOTE]
>
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled per organization.** Everything in the
> four sections below is behind that ga
te, enforced server-side. If it is not\n> on for your organization, the reads generally return empty and every **write**\n> — crea
ting a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a study,\n> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message naming the feat

ure, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
>
> Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because every one of them
\n> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal run, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal or swarm (each one

's `DELETE`). An
> organization that loses access can still stop what is running and clean up
> what it authored.
>
> Ask us o
n [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you want it turned on.\n\n**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...
`, `.../goals...`,\n`.../swarms...`) — the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic character; a *
*goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\nunder it. Nothin

g here starts anything — launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../perso
nas` | List the project's personas |\n| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/
{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe
|\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../goals` | List the
project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this proj
ect |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `ite
rations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep pointing
at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (a
ccepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's d
efaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their own values |\n| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals

under it stay launchable |

**Swarms — generation** — drafts a model writes for you. Both routes return
candidates and **persis
t nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create\nroutes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempotency-Key` — a cal
l\nwith no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and offering one would imply the\ndrafts are stable across retries when they are no

t.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grou
nded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `POST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so y

ou can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consume **no customer credits** — the model cost is on\
n> MCPJam. They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a\n> different wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retr
y in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for
the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, resets at UTC midnight). All three carry\n> `Retry-After` — hon
or it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every one: buying credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a

loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms — runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,
`.../goal-ru

ns/...`) — launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/run
s` | That goal's runs, newest first |\n| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers `202` — the fan-out has started, not
finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a differen
t actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is created. The response can report `funding` (`spon
sored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts`
|\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-ru
ns/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |\n\nThree things

worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a
 r
etry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` and start
